Subject: Region anchoring + purge lifecycle questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: NexusBank is evaluating Redwood Dedicated and we need to confirm a few things about region anchoring (we call it 'pinning') and how data is erased at the tenant level. Our procurement team will require concrete answers for the security review.

Can you confirm the following?
1) When a Dedicated instance is "anchored" to a region, does all customer data (model weights, KV caches, logs, snapshots) remain within that region and its AZs only, or are there any control-plane artefacts that transit other regions?
2) For tenant-level deletion, what's the end-to-end timeline and evidence we can expect (delete request -> confirm wipe -> persistent snapshot removal)?
3) Are backups/replicas ever stored outside the anchored region for DR? If yes, how do you manage access/controls?

We're aiming to present the answers to our InfoSec committee next Wednesday. Anything you can share in writing would be great.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Senior Cloud Security Engineer
NexusBank

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (customer ops) to provide the technical and operational details. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a short write-up and a diagram for your committee.

High level:
- Anchor = compute + storage + runtime artifacts are constrained to the pinned region.
- Control plane metadata (customer record, billing usage) is stored in our control plane; for Dedicated customers we offer an option to keep the control plane in a region-localized control plane (Private mode) — otherwise control-plane telemetry may be in a central region.
- Tenant deletion is a multi-step workflow: soft-delete flag -> KV + object purge -> snapshot deletion -> cryptographic key rotation; typical completion SLA is 72 hours for logical wipe and 14 days for all persistent snapshot purging depending on retention/archival windows.

Karthik / Marissa: can you confirm the DR backup policy (any cross-region replicas by default?) and whether we can produce an attestation package for NexusBank (runbook + signed timestamps)?

Best,

Alex / team —

Providing the infra specifics here. I've kept this focused on the Dedicated offering:

1) Data locality: all runtime data (model files, KV cache, generated artifacts, request logs stored for the dedicated retention window) are persisted on disks provisioned in the anchored region. No automatic cross-region replication for active volumes.

2) Control plane: for Dedicated customers we offer two options:
   - Hosted control plane (default): metadata + metrics are stored in our central control plane (US primary). We can sign an agreement to limit telemetry retention for NexusBank.
   - Regional control plane (enterprise/private): control plane endpoints deployed inside your region/VPC — in this mode control-plane metadata remains region-bound.

3) Backups/DR: we take scheduled snapshot backups. By default, snapshots for Dedicated clusters remain in-region and are encrypted using keys that are region-scoped. Cross-region replication is not enabled by default. If a customer requests an explicit DR replication to a secondary region, we treat it as a configuration option with contractual controls and KMS policy restrictions.

4) Deletion workflow (stepwise):
   - Request acknowledged (T0)
   - Soft-delete mark + pause ingestion (T+<1h)
   - Evict KV cache and delete active objects (T+<24h)
   - Delete snapshots and compacted backups (T+72h default)
   - KMS key rotation and final evidence bundle (T+7-14 days depending on snapshot retention)

Evidence we can provide: purge logs, snapshot manifest showing deletion, signed timestamp of key rotation, and an ops runbook. For regulated customers we can add a signed attestation and a short live run-through with our ops team.

I've attached the tenant purge runbook v2 and a simple region-anchor diagram.

Alex — quick answers for the InfoSec packet below (feel free to copy):

Q: Are PII identifiers written to the hosted control plane?
A: The hosted control plane stores tenant IDs and non-PII usage metadata by default. No raw customer PII (names, SSNs, account numbers) are written. If NexusBank requires stricter controls we can redact tenant identifiers from the hosted control plane or enable the regional control plane option.

Q: Does the 72h snapshot deletion SLA change if snapshots are moved to archive?
A: Archived snapshots are retained per the backup retention policy. If a snapshot has already been moved to an archival tier (cold storage) the deletion workflow can take up to 14 days because of archive retrieval windows. We include the archival window in the SLA calculation and can provide a custom retention window in contract.

Q: Lead time for attestation / ops run-through?
A: We can schedule an evidence session within 5 business days after a PO. For an untimed attestation (no PO) expect 10 business days. The attestation includes signed logs, snapshot manifests, and a live walkthrough of the deletion run.

If that looks good I'll prep a one-page Q&A and attach the relevant artifacts.

-rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
